subject: Audit dependency & cloud scope — clarifying shared responsibilities
messages:
From: Sara Lee <compliance@stormtech.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II + clarifying cloud provider coverage

Hi Michael / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. StormTech is moving forward with a security review for a PII-handling integration and we need a few items to complete our evidence package:

- The most recent SOC 2 Type II report for Redwood Inference (covering the period ending in 2025).
- A short statement on how Redwood treats your cloud infrastructure provider(s) for SOC purposes — specifically, do you rely on the cloud vendor's SOC report for infrastructure controls, or do you treat that as a complementary report (i.e., shared responsibility)?
- A current list of subprocessors that handle customer data (we are particularly interested in the managed database and logging providers).

Also: our auditor asked whether there are any service dependencies that are excluded from Redwood's attestation (e.g., managed DB or CDN). If you can confirm which components are in-scope vs out-of-scope for the report that would be very helpful.

Can you send the SOC 2 and a one-page clarification letter by next Tuesday (2026-10-06)? If some items require a short follow-up, that's fine — just let us know expected delivery dates.

Best,
Sara Lee
Senior Compliance Manager
StormTech Inc.

---
Attachment: none

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <compliance@stormtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + clarifying cloud provider coverage

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:

- We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report for the 2025 period.
- Redwood takes a shared-responsibility stance: control coverage for data plane compute, storage, and network configuration is a mix of Redwood internal controls and cloud-provider controls. We rely on the cloud vendor's SOC report for infrastructure-level controls (physical security, hypervisor, network fabric) while our SOC 2 attestation covers application-level controls, access provisioning, encryption in transit & at rest, and change management for our serving runtime.
- We will attach the current subprocessor inventory; it includes our managed DB provider and logging provider as covered subprocessors.

I want to confirm one thing for your auditor: when you say "excluded dependencies," do you mean services that are explicitly out of scope for our SOC 2 (i.e., Redwood does not assert controls for them), or third-party services that are described but relied upon (i.e., covered via the vendor's own attestations)?

We aim to get the SOC 2 PDF and the short clarifying statement to you by EOD Monday (2026-10-05). If the auditor needs a formal attestation letter that references the cloud vendor's report, we can coordinate with the cloud vendor security contact — copying Marissa to help coordinate.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Sara / Michael,

Attaching the two files that should cover your immediate needs: a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary (full report is on our secure portal; we'll share a controlled copy if you need it) and our latest subprocessor inventory CSV. A couple of notes:

- The SOC 2 summary highlights that infrastructure-level controls are covered by our cloud providers' SOC reports (we rely on those for physical and infrastructure security). We explicitly call out which infrastructure services are considered relied-upon services.
- For services we manage (inference runtime, tokenization pipeline, auth), Redwood is fully in-scope.

If StormTech's auditor requires a formal letter stating that Redwood's control coverage is "inclusive" of the managed DB (i.e., Redwood asserts controls over DB configuration and access), please flag that specifically — we may need to coordinate with the DB vendor for a short vendor confirmation note.

Thanks — received the attachments and the inventory. A couple of quick follow-ups from our auditor:

1) They want explicit wording confirming the audit period dates covered by the SOC 2 (start/end). I see the summary references 2025 but requests the exact ISO date range.
2) For the managed database: the auditor prefers a short vendor confirmation (1–2 paragraphs) that the vendor's controls were in place during the SOC 2 period and that Redwood's DB configuration controls were in-effect.

Can you provide the exact SOC period (ISO dates) and say whether Redwood can obtain the vendor confirmation, or alternatively provide a statement of Redwood's control activity around DB access/configuration during the SOC 2 period?

If you can send those by EOD Wednesday (2026-10-06) that will keep us on schedule.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lee <compliance@stormtech.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II + clarifying cloud provider coverage

Hi Sara — looping in to provide the specifics you requested.

- SOC 2 Type II period: 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z through 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z (the report in the portal is for that full calendar-year period).

- Managed database: Redwood classifies the managed DB as a subprocessor. During the SOC 2 period Redwood maintained the following controls related to DB configuration and access (sample controls):
  * RBAC enforced via central identity provider; privileged roles require MFA and scoped temporary elevation.
  * Automated configuration baseline enforcement via IaC templates and drift detection; deviations trigger change-review workflows.
  * Database audit logging enabled and retained according to our data-retention policy; logs are forwarded to our logging provider which is listed in the subprocessor inventory.

We can request a short vendor confirmation from the managed DB provider that their infrastructure controls were in place for the SOC 2 period. Historically those vendor confirmations are a brief note and not a formal SOC report replacement — if StormTech's auditor needs the vendor note we will reach out and share what we receive.

If you want the vendor confirmation routed directly to your auditor, tell us the contact and we will coordinate. Otherwise, we'll include a statement of Redwood control activity (summary above) alongside a note that the DB provider maintains its own attestation.

-Jonas Weber
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
